page_title: {SRE} in the Small and in the Large

sources.entry: SRE in the Small and in the Large

summary.name: SRE in the Small and in the Large
summary.one_liner: A 2016 USENIX LISA closing plenary talk by Niall Murphy and Todd Underwood (Google) arguing that Site Reliability Engineering principles apply to small organizations as well as large ones.
use_cases: Deciding whether a small team should adopt SRE practices
Making the case to management for reliability practices
Understanding SRE principles beyond large-scale systems
Reviewing conference material on operations culture
summary.what_it_does: ["Presents a talk arguing that SRE is not only for very large organizations. The speakers say its core principles apply equally to a single-person startup and to Google. The page describes the talk's aim: to show evidence that might persuade a boss to adopt standard SRE practices. The page itself contains only the abstract and citation details, not the slides, video, or the content of the principles themselves."]
notable: Speakers are Niall Murphy and Todd Underwood of Google
Part of USENIX LISA 2016 in Boston, MA, held as the closing plenary
USENIX open access policy: post-event video, audio, and slides are free
caveats: Page contains only the abstract; the detailed principles and evidence are not included in the page text
